title: Policy on Students Getting Hurt on School Premises
what_it_is: Policy on Students Getting Hurt on School Premises

sections.label: School safety and injury response
sections.summary: Schools check safety, teach safety skills, render first aid, seek consent for treatment, call ambulances for serious injury, and provide accident insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools do their due diligence to ensure their activities and activity venues are safe so as to minimise the risk of injury.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools proactively perform regular checks on building infrastructure and equipment to ensure they are safe and teach students safety-related skills.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: If a student sustains light injury, staff trained in First Aid will render assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: If medical treatment is required, the school will seek parental consent to send the student to a nearby clinic or the parents may prefer to do so themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For serious injury, the school will call an ambulance to send the student to the nearest hospital and inform the parents.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: All our students are covered by Student Accident Protection Plans purchased by the schools to cover medical expenses incurred.

sections.label: Support for injured students
sections.summary: For CCA injuries, schools help students get treatment and work with insurance companies through the claims and recovery process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: What happens is that if there are injuries sustained while the students are, let us say, doing the CCAs, we will work with the student to see how we can facilitate; one aspect is in terms of getting treatment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The other aspect is to see how we can work with the insurance companies to look through and journey with the students on the process of the claims and how this process of recovery can be made together.
